beats.text: He read one chapter a week. Standing up.
Near Charminar, a footpath book stall. Every Sunday a boy read one chapter, then put the book back. He couldn't afford it.
Nine Sundays. Nine chapters. The old seller never said a word. He just never sold that book.
The tenth Sunday, the boy didn't come. Or the next. Or the one after that.
Twenty years later, a parcel reached the stall: a new novel, signed "For the man who kept chapter ten for me."
beats.small: The author's name was the boy's.

end.text: Who kept a book for you?
